newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada police receive two Bre-X fraud complaints.
newsitem.headline: Canada police receive two Bre-X fraud complaints.

text.p: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) said on Wednesday that it had received two official complaints regarding Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd and the Busang gold scandal.
The RCMP said in a statement that it received a letter of complaint from Bre-X Chief Executive David Walsh alleging that a fraud was perpetrated against Bre-X.
"No suspect was identified in that letter," the RCMP said.
The RCMP said it also received a complaint from the Ontario Securities Commission (OSC), alleging a fraud involving Bre-X.
The OSC is Canada's top securities regulator.
The RCMP said investigators were meeting this week to discuss the complaints and decide which direction will be taken.

The Busang discovery -- touted by Calgary, Alberta-based Bre-X as the richest find of the century -- was falsified on a scale "without precedent in the history of mining," according to a report issued late on Sunday by consultant Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd.
Since then Bre-X's stock -- once valued at more than C$6 billion ($4.4 billion) -- has collapsed to pennies a share and class action suits loom against the embattled miner.
After Wednesday's close, the Toronto Stock Exchange delisted shares in Bre-X. The stock closed up 0.005 at C$0.09 on massive volume of 20 million shares today.
